docs.text: BlendReal™ Spaceship Traffic Procedural Blender add-on for spaceship traffic — automatically generates lane/intersection networks, avoids buildings by pre-checking real gaps between them so every ship flies a single straight line with zero mid-flight direction changes, and performs true ship-to-ship avoidance using a Space-Time Reservation system. Includes a flight path toolkit (7 NURBS Path presets + Follow Curve for Mesh or Camera), a shared Camera Track-To / Camera Shake / Bake Animation / Restore Constraint toolkit, mesh utilities, and an optional engine exhaust effect export to Unreal Niagara via BlendReal™. The add-on operates in Standalone Mode — Unreal Engine is not required — all traffic features run entirely within Blender. Alternatively, the Spaceship Trail (Export to UE) feature requires the BlendReal™ - Cinematic Pipeline UE5 add-on to automatically transfer Niagara parameter values into UE. ⚙️System Requirements Operating System: Windows 10/11 64-bit Blender : 4.5, 5.0, or 5.2 (LTS) Unreal Engine is not required for the main traffic features BlendReal™ (separate add-on) is required to use the Spaceship Trail feature 🛠️Installation In Blender, go to Edit > Preferences > Add-ons Click Install from Disk... and select the .zip file Tick the checkbox next to BlendReal™ Spaceship Traffic to enable the add-on Open the Sidebar (press N ) in the 3D Viewport and find the Spaceship Traffic tab 🔷Basic Workflow Prepare Your Models : have your spaceship models ready (in .blend format, with one or several ships per file), along with building/obstacle models in the scene Create Collections : in the 📦 Streams & Collections section, click 🗂 Create Collections (Ships + Buildings) to automatically create the required Collections with the correct names (automatically based on whether "Split Into 3 Separate Streams" is on/off) Import Ships : still in 📦 Streams & Collections — select the folder containing the spaceship .blend files in Ship File Folder , choose which stream to import them into ( Import Into Stream ), then click 📥 Import Ships From Folder . Ships can all sit on top of each other at the origin at this point — Generate Traffic will redistribute them automatically Add Buildings to the Collection : manually drag and drop the building objects into the created Collection in the Outliner Click ⚡ Auto-Fill From Ship Sizes (inside the 🛣️ Lanes section) — this is the recommended first step : the add-on automatically computes most of the lane/altitude spacing values based on the actual size of your imported ships instead of you guessing numbers by hand. Everything stays freely editable afterward — Generate Traffic will NOT overwrite these values Preview the layout (optional) : also inside 🛣️ Lanes , click 👁 Create ShipProxy , then adjust the Lane/Streams/Formation fields to see whether the ship placeholder boxes are arranged the way you want (see Live Layout Preview below) Click ▶ Generate Traffic — the add-on automatically generates animation for all ships, with real building and ship avoidance To start over: click ✕ Clear Animation To view the system report: click 🔍 Check Collections (found inside Streams & Collections; output is displayed in the System Console) 💡 Tip for new users : if you don't want to hand-tune every parameter, simply follow Import Ships → Auto-Fill From Ship Sizes → Generate Traffic and you'll immediately get a reasonable traffic layout. The sections below are only needed when you want to fine-tune things further. ✨Detailed Features (The sections below are listed in the exact order they appear in the add-on's real Sidebar panel.) 🛤️ NURBS Path Presets 7 built-in shapes, spawned right at the selected object's location (or at the 3D Cursor if nothing is selected): Straight , Arc , Loop , S-Curve , Zigzag , Spiral , Figure-8 . After creation, adjust the parameters in the "Adjust Last Operation" panel (bottom-left): - Size — overall length (Straight/Arc/S-Curve/Zigzag) or radius (Loop/Spiral/Figure-8) - Points — number of NURBS control points, higher = smoother curve - Forward Axis — which local axis the path primarily travels along - Arc Angle — Arc only: how many degrees the arc sweeps - Amplitude / Wave Cycles — S-Curve/Zigzag only: how far the path swings side to side, and how many oscillations - Turns / Height — Spiral only: number of full rotations and total distance travelled Follow Curve : select exactly 1 mesh or camera + 1 curve (any order), then click — automatically adds a Follow Path constraint (named "BlendReal Follow Path"), along with Curve Resolution (how smooth the curve itself is). You only need to keyframe the 2 values that appear right below while that object is selected: Follow Path Distance (actual distance in Blender units, not a 0–1 ratio) and Follow Path Tilt (additional banking angle). 🎥 Camera-specific behavior : if the followed object is a Camera, Follow Path only drives its POSITION along the curve — it does not rotate the camera to match the curve's tangent, and Follow Path Tilt has no visible effect. This is on purpose: it leaves 100% of the aim/rotation to whatever the Camera already has (typically a Track To constraint from Create Camera Track-To Constraint , see the Bake Animation section below), so the camera keeps looking exactly where you pointed it while still flying along the curve. ⚠️ The Bake Auto Bank feature (automatically computing the banking angle from the curve's curvature) is currently an internal work-in-progress (WIP) and is not shown in the panel in this build — for now, adjust Tilt manually via keyframes. 🎬 Bake Animation (Location/Rotation/Scale) Remove Constraint After Bake — after baking, automatically removes the original Constraint(s) (Follow Path, Track To...) to avoid double-transform conflicts; disable this if you still need to edit the Constraint(s) afterward Bake Animation — bakes Location/Rotation/Scale of any selected Mesh, Camera, or Empty into real keyframes with one click, automatically backing up every supported Constraint present on the object before baking (e.g. a Camera using both Follow Path + Track To together — not just one of them) Restore Baked Constraint — restores all the original Constraint(s) + Target(s) + Action from before the last bake (only works on objects previously baked via the button above); this data is shared with BlendReal™ - Cinematic Pipeline UE5 , so baking in one add-on can be restored from the other Create Camera Track-To Constraint — one click creates a Camera + a target Empty (named "CameraTarget") with a Track To constraint already set up between them (more stable than Damped Track during live preview); shared feature also found in BlendReal™ - Cinematic Pipeline UE5 Add Camera Shake — adds a short, keyframed handheld-style shake to the selected Camera starting at the current frame, with Amplitude , Frequency , Pulses , and Target Shake Ratio (if the Camera has a Track To / Damped Track constraint, its target Empty shakes too — phase-shifted by 1/4 cycle so the aim direction wobbles naturally instead of staying locked dead-on target; set to 0 to shake only the Camera). Re-running this on an overlapping frame range replaces the previous shake there automatically 🔧 Mesh Utilities — standalone, no BlendReal™ required Apply Rotation / Apply Scale — applies in batch to multiple selected meshes at once, keeping the other 2 values unchanged (Location is always preserved by both buttons) Apply Naming (Island/Building/Landscape) — batch renames using a standard prefix, opening a dialog with: Type — Floating Island ( Island_ ) / Building ( Building_ ) / Landscape ( Landscape_ ) / Custom Prefix (your own prefix, no automatic Tag/Collision assignment) Base Name — the name part after the prefix (e.g. "FloatingIsland" → Island_FloatingIsland01 , 02 ...) Custom Prefix — only used when Type = Custom Start Index / Digit Count — the starting number and zero-padding digit count (2 digits: 01, 02...; 3 digits: 001, 002...) Fix Normals Per UV Island — recalculates normals per UV island in a radial outward direction (based on the object's center of mass, independent of topology) — handles cases where Blender's default Recalculate Outside / Merge+Recalculate fail Create Proxy Collision (Convex Hull) — duplicates meshes named with this convention, splits them by connected "island" pieces, with 2 Method options: Convex Hull Per Piece (recommended) — always clean regardless of how broken the source mesh is, preserves concavities between pieces Voxel Remesh (fallback) — rebuilds the surface via a distance field, with extra [Voxel] Resolution , [Voxel] Adaptivity , [Voxel] Weld Vertices Before Remesh , [Voxel] Merge Distance parameters The result is named so UE automatically recognizes it as Collision 📦 Streams & Collections Split Into 3 Separate Streams (Civilian / Cargo / Military) — on (default): each ship type is pulled from its own Collection, flying its own altitude band and speed factor, never mixing, while still sharing one Space-Time Reservation ledger so they still avoid each other correctly at stream crossing points. Off: falls back to a single shared ship Collection Civilian / Cargo / Military Collection + a Speed × multiplier for each stream (default Civilian ×0.85, Cargo ×0.6, Military ×1.35 — applied on top of the shared Minimum/Maximum Speed) Distance Between Streams — the horizontal offset (top view, X axis) between the 3 stream areas: Civilian on the left, Cargo in the middle, Military on the right, each with its own non-overlapping intersection grid Building Collection — the Collection containing buildings/obstacles 🗂 Create Collections (Ships + Buildings) — automatically creates the required Collections (using the names set in the fields above) if they don't already exist 🔍 Check Collections — prints a system report to the System Console Import Into Stream + Ship File Folder (.blend) + 📥 Import Ships From Folder — batch imports every ship from all .blend files in a folder into the Collection of the chosen stream, with a progress bar + elapsed time counter in the viewport, automatically skipping Cameras/Lights, and remembering previously imported files to prevent duplicates 🚦 Intersection Grid (per stream) Number Of Rows (Y) / Number Of Columns (X) — the number of rows/columns of the intersection grid. The actual number of intersections is ALWAYS Rows × Columns (since every road axis runs the full length of the grid, you can't get an arbitrary intersection count like 3, 5, 7 unless the grid has only 1 row/column) Distance Between Adjacent Intersections — the distance between the centers of 2 adjacent intersections (same row or same column) 🛣️ Lanes (per row/column) Lanes Per Road Cluster — the number of lanes in EACH row/column of the grid (not the total lane count for the whole scene) — always use an EVEN number, since every 2 adjacent lanes pair up into 1 two-way "road" Number Of Altitude Levels — the number of altitude (Z) levels flying simultaneously within one stream When 3 Streams is on, the 6 spacing fields below get separate columns for Civilian / Cargo / Military : Dist. Lanes (Distance Between Lanes) — the distance between 2 neighboring two-way "roads" Dist. Levels (Distance Between Levels) — the spacing between 2 adjacent altitude levels Lowest Alt Z (Lowest Level Altitude) — the lowest altitude, used as the base the levels above stack on Hor. Offset (Horizontal Offset Between Levels) — the alternating horizontal offset between even/odd levels, for a more natural layout 2-Way Dist. (Two-Way Distance Within 1 Road) — the distance between the 2 opposing lanes within the SAME road — should be set MUCH smaller than Distance Between Lanes Extra Dist. (Extra Distance Between 2 Roads) — an EXTRA gap (on top of Distance Between Lanes) between 2 adjacent lane pairs ⚡ Auto-Fill From Ship Sizes (recommended): a one-time action — automatically fills Distance Between Lanes / Distance Between Levels / Two-Way Distance / Extra Distance for each stream based on its largest ship's radius, and lowers the Vertical/Horizontal Step Ratio to a safe value (≤0.4) so Vertical Staggered Slot never gets clamped, regardless of ship size. Lowest Level Altitude Z is stacked in order Civilian → Cargo → Military (each step taking the LARGER of Distance Between Streams or the stream-below's own vertical span) — guaranteeing no altitude overlap between streams without an oversized gap for normal-sized fleets. Horizontal Offset Between Levels is copied as-is from Civilian (purely cosmetic, not size-related). Everything stays freely editable afterward — Generate Traffic will NOT overwrite these values again. 👁️ Live Layout Preview (lives inside the Lanes section) 👁 Create ShipProxy — creates lightweight proxy boxes sized exactly to each ship, at each ship's current position; the real ships are temporarily hidden Once the boxes exist, adjust any Lane/Streams/Formation field — the layout updates live on the boxes You can also click ▶ Generate Traffic while previewing — the add-on runs the full collision-avoidance pass ON THE BOXES (faster than running it on real, detailed-mesh ships), while still using the ships' REAL radius for safety calculations ✅ Apply ShipProxy — once you're happy with it, brings back the real ships and applies the final result to them 💡 This is a tool for previewing a reasonable layout — the final, accurate result always comes from clicking ▶ Generate Traffic on the real ships (via Apply ShipProxy, or directly if you're not using the preview). ✈️ Staggered Formation Staggered Slots — Horizontal / — Vertical (Z) — the number of horizontal/vertical offset positions in a lane's staggered formation, letting multiple ships share a lane without overlapping Vertical / Horizontal Step Ratio — the vertical (Z) step = this ratio × the horizontal step — usually kept below 1, since the Z gap between levels is limited Group Ships By Size — OFF (default, same as previous versions): the staggered step is computed once from the largest ship radius in the WHOLE stream. ON: ships are first grouped by size (see Size Grouping Threshold (%) — e.g. 50 = up to 1.5x that group's smallest radius), tightening the Staggered Formation spacing per lane based on whichever ships actually ended up there, instead of always sizing for the stream's single largest ship ℹ️ When buildings exist in the scene , Gap-Fit (see Building Avoidance below) already assigns ships to lanes by their real size automatically — Group Ships By Size no longer decides which lane a ship goes to in that case, but it still tightens the Staggered Formation spacing per lane the same way described above. ⚡ Speed & Timing Minimum Speed / Maximum Speed — the random speed-factor range applied to each ship (further multiplied by the per-stream Speed ×) Frames To Cross Scene (Speed 1.0) — the reference number of frames to travel the full scene length at speed factor 1.0 Total Animation Frames — every ship's animation spans exactly from frame 0 to this value ⚠️ Important note when increasing speed : if you push speed much higher relative to Total Animation Frames, a ship may finish flying its entire lane in just a few dozen frames while the displayed timeline is several hundred or thousand frames long — that ship will "flash by" quickly, then sit FROZEN for most of the remaining timeline, making it look like "most ships aren't moving." This isn't a bug — if you want to see many ships moving clearly throughout the video, keep speed moderate or shorten Total Animation Frames accordingly. 🌐 Scene Size Scene Radius — ships depart from and arrive beyond this radius Push Back Beyond Boundary — the extra distance ships start out/end beyond the Scene Radius boundary 🏢 Building Avoidance Every ship flies exactly 1 straight line, with zero direction changes mid-flight — building avoidance is entirely decided before a ship starts moving, not reacted to along the way: For every lane, the add-on sweeps its full length and works out the narrowest real gap between buildings that a ship would have to pass through — accounting for the Building Collision Margin AND the worst-case sideways reach of the Staggered Formation (so a ship can never be nudged into a building it was assigned to safely clear) Each ship is only assigned to a lane whose gap is wide enough for its own width, widest ships first, spread across the least-used valid lanes If NO lane in the grid is wide enough for a ship (e.g. an oversized capital ship in a dense building cluster), the add-on automatically creates a Boundary Lane just outside the entire building cluster's footprint and routes it there instead — guaranteed clear, at the same altitude levels as normal traffic A building sitting directly on a lane's centerline (a true dead end, not just a tight squeeze) removes that lane from consideration entirely, the same way as an insufficient gap Building Collision Margin — the safety buffer kept around every building's actual bounds, used throughout the gap calculation above 🛸 Ship-Ship Collision Avoidance (Outer Edge) Safety Distance (Ship Hull Outer Edge) — the minimum gap measured from the ship's OUTER HULL edge (not center-to-center) — the add-on automatically adds each ship's actual radius (from its bounding box) both when checking space-time conflicts AND when computing the staggered formation's offset step. Increasing this value does NOT stretch ships further apart along the lane — it only widens the staggered formation grid Fallback Delay Step (Frames) — ONLY used when 2 ships would land on the exact same staggered-formation slot (the primary avoidance mechanism is spatial, not time-based) Max Delay Attempts — how many fallback delay attempts before accepting the conflict After Generate Traffic , the add-on clearly reports the number of ships that could not fully avoid collisions + suggests which parameter to increase. ⚙️ Options Random Seed — change to get a different ship layout Ship Nose Axis (Local) — the local axis the ship's nose points along (enable local axis display in the N-panel or Viewport Overlays > Axes to see the correct axis; change this if the ship flies "nose backwards" or "sideways" after Generate) Interpolation Type — Linear (100% match when exported to UE via BlendReal, in both export modes) or Bezier (smoother, with ease in/out — but only matches exactly when BlendReal uses "Every Frame" mode) 🔥 Spaceship Trail (Export to UE) — optional, requires BlendReal™ - Cinematic Pipeline UE5 Enable Spaceship Trail — the master switch for the trail feature Niagara System Path (UE) — the Content Browser path to the pre-built Niagara System in UE; can be found via Trail Package Folder + Scan for Trail Systems to automatically scan and pick Trail Height Ratio / Trail Side Ratio — where the trail attaches, vertically and side-to-side, scaled to each ship's OWN actual size Ribbon Width Ratio — the ribbon width, also scaled to each ship's own actual size Niagara Look (User Parameters) : Hot Phase Duration (how long the white-hot → red glow lasts before fading to smoke), Noise Intensity (turbulence), Trail Lifetime (total trail length in time), Trail Opacity , plus individual trail colors per stream (or one shared color when 3 Streams is off) 🔄 Refresh Ship List , Include/Exclude lists (pick individual ships or whole Collections, live-linked — Exclude always wins), Recompute ALL Ships (OFF by default — safe, only computes ships without data yet; turn on to force a full recompute, with confirmation first) Compute & Preview Trail Points — automatically computes trail attachment points from each ship's bounding box + Nose Axis, shown as draggable Empty markers (paired markers auto-sync) Clear Trail Preview Markers , Apply Marker Positions to Export Data — writes the final positions into the export data 📋 Config Preset Save every current parameter value as a custom-named preset ( 💾 Save Preset ), then Load Preset / Delete anytime — switch instantly between different configurations (stored as JSON). 📄License & Source Code You should have received a copy of the GNU General Public License along with this program. If not, see http://www.gnu.org/licenses/ . The installation package includes the add-on's Python ( .py ) source files packaged in a .zip archive. 💬Support For any questions or update requests, please contact us through the BlendReal™ Discord Support channel. ❓FAQs ✅ Does this add-on work independently? Yes — all traffic simulation (lanes, building avoidance, ship avoidance, and animation) runs entirely within Blender. Only the Exhaust Trail feature requires the BlendReal™ - Cinematic Pipeline UE5 add-on. ✅ When do I need to use it together with the BlendReal™ - Cinematic Pipeline UE5 add-on? When you need the Spaceship Trail feature ( Export to UE ) to transfer Niagara parameter values into UE. ✅ Ships flying in the wrong direction (upside down/sideways) after Generate Traffic? Change the Ship Nose Axis value to match the actual nose direction of your ship model. ✅ After Generate Traffic, it reports "X ship(s) COULD NOT fully avoid collisions"? Increase Staggered Slots Horizontal/Vertical , or increase Max Delay Attempts / Fallback Delay Step . ✅ Is there a way to optimize the setup time for the add-on parameters? Yes — the fastest way is to click ⚡ Auto-Fill From Ship Sizes (inside the Lanes section) right after importing your ships; the add-on will automatically compute most of the lane spacing based on your actual ship sizes. If you'd still like to fine-tune by hand, just focus on a few key parameters: Ship speed (Speed & Timing), Distance Between Streams (Streams & Collections) Lowest Level Altitude (Z), Distance Between Levels (Lanes) Distance Between Adjacent Intersections (Intersection Grid) ✅ Is the layout shown by Live Layout Preview (Create ShipProxy) the final result? Not exactly — it's a quick way to preview whether the spacing, altitude levels, and density look reasonable before running the real thing. The final, accurate result (real collision avoidance + real animation) always comes from clicking ▶ Generate Traffic on the real ships. ✅ Where is Bake Auto Bank (automatic banking based on the flight path's curvature)? This feature is currently an internal work-in-progress and is not yet shown in the panel in this build — for now, adjust Follow Path Tilt manually via keyframes to create a banking effect. ✅ Some ships fly all the way around a whole cluster of buildings instead of through it — is that a bug? No — this is the Boundary Lane fallback described in Building Avoidance above, working as intended. It only triggers for ships whose width can't fit through ANY real gap in that lane (accounting for the Staggered Formation's sideways reach). If you'd rather see more ships weaving between buildings, try lowering Staggered Slots — Horizontal , or spacing buildings further apart in your scene. ✅ Why are there Camera Track-To / Camera Shake buttons in a spaceship traffic add-on? They're the same Camera tools also found in BlendReal™ - Cinematic Pipeline UE5 , included here too so you don't need to switch add-ons for basic camera work. Both add-ons share the same Bake/Restore data format, so a camera baked in one can be restored in the other. BlendReal™ Spaceship Traffic Tutorial Videos 1.BlendReal Camera System: Track-To, Follow Curve & Camera Shake - 100% Consistent in Blender & UE5 The same Camera toolkit shared with BlendReal™ - Cinematic Pipeline UE5 — set up a Track-To camera, send it flying along any curve, add a handheld shake, bake it, and export straight to Unreal Engine 5 with a 1:1 match. Create Camera Track-To Constraint. One click spawns a Camera + a target Empty ("CameraTarget") already linked with a Track To constraint — more stable to preview live than a Damped Track constraint. Follow Curve (Camera). Attach the Camera to any of the 7 NURBS Path presets (or a hand-drawn curve) — Follow Path only drives its POSITION along the curve, leaving 100% of the aim/rotation to the Track To constraint, so the camera keeps looking exactly where you pointed it while flying the path. Bake Animation. Converts the live Camera Track-To + Follow Curve setup into real keyframes with one click, backing up every Constraint present (Follow Path + Track To together) so nothing is lost. Restore Baked Constraint. Brings back the exact original Constraint(s) + Target(s) afterward, so you can re-edit the camera move and re-bake instead of starting over. Add Camera Shake. Layers a short handheld-style shake on top of the Camera's existing Location animation — Amplitude, Frequency, Pulses, plus Target Shake Ratio so the Track-To target wobbles too (phase-shifted, so the aim direction drifts naturally instead of staying locked dead-on target). Export to Unreal Engine 5. The Camera appears in the UE Outliner automatically organized, with zero manual setup — matching the Blender camera's position, rotation, and timing exactly. 2.Basic Traffic Setup & Saving Presets From importing ships to generating a full traffic simulation, then saving your setup as a reusable preset. Ship Collection / Building Collection. Two named Collections that define which objects in your scene count as "ships" versus "buildings" for the entire system. Create Collections (Ships + Buildings) . One click creates both collections if they don't exist yet. Import Ships From Folder. Batch-imports every ship .blend file in a chosen folder straight into the Ship Collection, instead of appending each one by hand. Generate Traffic. The main button — runs the entire pipeline (lanes, avoidance, animation) in one pass and animates every ship at once, based on every other setting across the addon's panels. Clear Animation. Removes the generated animation so you can regenerate cleanly after changing settings, instead of it stacking on top of the previous result. Check Collections. A read-only sanity check that reports how many ships and buildings your current collections actually contain before you commit to Generate Traffic. Save / Load / Delete Preset. Save your entire configuration — every panel, not just this one — as a named preset, and switch between different setups for different scenes in seconds via Choose & Load Preset / Choose & Delete Preset. 3.Configuring Traffic Streams & Lane Grid Split your traffic into 3 independently-tuned streams and control exactly how many lanes, intersections, and altitude levels your traffic system generates. Split Into 3 Separate Streams (Civilian / Cargo / Military). Routes ships into 3 separate collections, each with its own Speed Factor (Civilian 0.85, Cargo 0.6, Military 1.35 by default) and its own non-overlapping lanes, while still avoiding each other at intersections. Distance Between Streams. Keeps the 3 streams physically separated so they never fly through one another. Per-Stream Lane Tuning. Each stream (and the default single-stream mode) has its own Lanes Per Road Cluster, Distance Between Lanes, Number of Altitude Levels, Distance Between Levels, Lowest Level Altitude, and Horizontal Offset Between Levels — so, for example, Cargo lanes can be spaced completely differently from Military lanes. Intersection Grid. Number of Rows/Columns and Distance Between Adjacent Intersections control how many intersections exist in your scene and how far apart they sit. Staggered Slots & Step Ratio. Staggered Slots — Horizontal/Vertical and the Vertical/Horizontal Step Ratio fine-tune how ships queue at intersections so they don't visibly bunch up. Group Ships By Size. An optional toggle (with its own Size Grouping Threshold %) that groups similarly-sized ships together, so a tiny fighter isn't forced into the same lane spacing as a capital ship. Auto-Fill From Ship Sizes. Automatically calculates sensible lane-spacing values by scanning the actual size of the ships already in your collection, instead of guessing numbers by hand. 4.Building & Ship Avoidance Explained See how BlendReal's raycast-based building avoidance and Space-Time Reservation ship avoidance work together. Gap-Fit Building Avoidance. Before any ship moves, the add-on sweeps every lane to find the narrowest real gap between buildings a ship passing through it would face, accounting for the Building Collision Margin (default 5.0) and the Staggered Formation's worst-case sideways reach — then only assigns ships to lanes wide enough for their own size, so every ship flies one straight line with zero mid-flight direction changes. Boundary Lane. Ships too wide for any real gap in the lane grid (or blocked outright by a building sitting on the centerline) are automatically routed around the entire building cluster instead, on an auto-generated lane placed just outside its footprint. Space-Time Reservation Ship Avoidance. This is the real avoidance engine, and it's the addon's core selling point: it doesn't offset ships randomly. It reserves each ship's exact path as a function of both position and frame (time), then checks every new ship's path for its closest distance to already-reserved paths within the overlapping time window — genuinely keeping a Safety Distance (Ship Hull Outer Edge) rather than guessing. Fallback Delay Step / Max Delay Attempts. If a ship's path still conflicts after checking, it's delayed by a set number of frames (Fallback Delay Step) and retried, up to Max Delay Attempts times, before the system reports a conflict it couldn't resolve. Random Seed. Makes the entire avoidance/generation result reproducible — running Generate Traffic again with the same seed gives you the exact same layout. 5.Flight Path Tools 7 built-in NURBS path presets plus Follow Curve and Bake Auto Bank for custom ship movement 7 NURBS Path Presets. Straight, Arc, Loop, S-Curve, Zigzag, Spiral, and Figure-8, each spawned at your active object's location (or the 3D Cursor), with shape-specific controls — Arc Angle for Arc, Amplitude/Wave Cycles for S-Curve and Zigzag, Turns/Height for Spiral. Follow Curve. Attaches a ship — or a Camera — to any of these paths (or a hand-drawn curve) as a Follow Path target. 6.Troubleshooting Fix ships flying in the wrong direction and resolve collision-avoidance warnings. Ship Nose Axis (Local). If ships fly upside-down or sideways after Generate Traffic, this tells the system which local axis on your ship model actually points "forward" — fixing the orientation without needing to re-model or re-orient every ship by hand. Staggered Slots / Max Delay Attempts (increase these). If you see a collision-avoidance warning after Generate Traffic, raising these two values gives the Space-Time Reservation system more room and more attempts to find a conflict-free path before it reports failure. Vertical Staggered Slot Step Capped. A second, separate warning that can appear after Generate Traffic — it means the Vertical Staggered Slot step a lane needs for its largest ship exceeded the safe cap for that stream (0.4× its Distance Between Levels), so the addon clamped it instead. Fix by raising Distance Between Levels, or lowering the Vertical/Horizontal Step Ratio. Spaceship Traffic Addon — UI Field Reference This guide walks through every field on the panel , in the exact order they appear in the 🚀 Spaceship Traffic panel (View3D > sidebar N > "Spaceship Traffic" tab). Use it to understand what a field does, or to figure out which field to adjust when troubleshooting an unusual result. How the addon works overall (read this first) The addon generates spaceship traffic in 3 main steps: Build the Intersection Grid — a row × column grid; each grid point is where "roads" cross. Build lanes on each row/column of the grid — each lane has a fixed flight direction ( +1 or -1 ), and lanes are offset from each other to form two-way "roads". Assign ships to lanes — if Buildings exist, the addon uses Gap-Fit : ships are only placed in a lane with enough real clearance (won't clip a building); if there are no buildings, ships are assigned via a simple round-robin. Animate — each ship flies a single straight path (no mid-flight steering), with staggered departure times so it looks natural, and collision avoidance against other ships via the Space-Time Reservation system. The most important button is ▶ Generate Traffic at the bottom of the panel — this is the ONLY place that guarantees a 100% accurate result. The live preview you see while typing into a Lanes/Formation field is only meant to show a reasonable layout while you adjust values, not a guaranteed-accurate result. 1. 🛤️ NURBS Path Presets A secondary toolset, not directly tied to the traffic system — used to quickly create a curve as a flight path for a single standalone object (not a whole traffic stream). Straight / Arc / Loop / S-Curve / Zigzag / Spiral / Figure-8 — Each button creates that curve shape, spawned at the currently selected object (or the 3D Cursor if nothing is selected). After clicking, adjust Size/Points/etc. in the "Adjust Last Operation" panel (bottom-left of the viewport). Follow Curve — Select 1 mesh/camera + 1 curve, then click — adds a "Follow Path" Constraint so that object follows the curve. Distance / Tilt (appear after Follow Path is added) — These are properties on the object itself (not addon fields) — drag to move the object along the curve, and to tilt it. Used to hand-keyframe motion along the path. Curve Resolution — Smoothness of the target curve — higher = smoother curve but heavier on performance. Note: this is a standalone tool and does not share any data with the main Generate Traffic system. 2. 🎬 Bake Animation (Location/Rotation/Scale) Remove Constraint After Bake (default: On) — After baking the animation to keyframes, automatically removes the original Constraint (Follow Path, Track To…) to prevent a double-transform conflict. Turn off if you still need to edit the Constraint afterward. Bake Animation (button) — Bakes the object's current animation into real keyframes (Location/Rotation/Scale). Restore Constraint (button) — Only works on objects previously baked via this exact button (or via the BlendReal_Core.py addon, since both addons share the same custom property key) — restores the original Constraint so it can be re-edited and re-baked. Create Camera Track To (button) — Quickly adds a Track To Constraint for a camera. Add Camera Shake (button) — Adds a camera shake effect. 3. 🔧 Mesh Utilities A set of mesh utilities, fully independent from the BlendReal_Core.py addon (no cross-calls — you can use this even if you only own one of the two addons). Apply Rotation / Apply Scale — Applies (bakes) the current rotation/scale into the base mesh, resetting the transform to 0/1 default. Apply Naming (Island/Building/Landscape) — Automatically renames objects following the standard Island/Building/Landscape naming convention. Fix Normals Per UV Island — Fixes normal direction separately for each UV island. Create Proxy Collision (Convex Hull) — Generates a simple collision mesh (convex hull) from the base mesh — used as lightweight collision when exporting to UE. 4. 📦 Streams & Collections This is where you declare which Collection ships are pulled from . Split Into 3 Separate Streams (Civilian / Cargo / Military) (default: On) — On: ships are pulled from 3 separate Collections , each type flying its own altitude (Z) band and speed, never mixing — while still sharing one Space-Time Reservation ledger, so they still avoid each other correctly at the points where two streams cross. Off: falls back to a single Collection , exactly like the old addon version (v6/v7). Civilian / Cargo / Military Collection (default: Spaceships_Civilian / Spaceships_Cargo / Spaceships_Military ) — Collection name holding each ship type (only shown when Split Into 3 Streams is on). Speed Factor — Civilian / Cargo / Military (default: 0.85 / 0.6 / 1.35) — An EXTRA multiplier applied on top of the random speed (Min/Max Speed under Speed & Timing) for that specific stream. Cargo ships are usually bigger & slower, hence a lower factor; Military ships are usually more compact & faster, hence a higher factor. Ship Collection (default: Spaceships ) — Collection holding the ships (only shown when Split Into 3 Streams is OFF). Building Collection (default: Buildings ) — Collection holding buildings/obstacles. If this Collection is empty or doesn't exist, the addon treats the scene as having NO buildings at all (the entire Gap-Fit building-avoidance mechanism is skipped). Create Collections (button) — Automatically creates the Collections using the names currently declared above (if they don't already exist). Check Collections (button) — Prints a quick diagnostic summary to the Console: ship count, building count, sizes of each — handy for double-checking your setup. Import Into Stream (default: Civilian) — When clicking "Import Ships From Folder", which stream's Collection the imported ships get added to (only shown when Split Into 3 Streams is on). Ship File Folder (.blend) — Path to a folder containing multiple .blend files, each holding 1 (or a few) ships — click the Import button below to append all of them into the Collection at once, no need to drag and drop each file. Import Ships From Folder (button) — Performs the bulk import described above. 5. 🚦 Intersection Grid (per stream) Defines the intersection grid — the number of crossing points between "roads". Number Of Rows (Y) (default: 3) — Number of horizontal rows in the intersection grid. Number Of Columns (X) (default: 3) — Number of vertical columns in the intersection grid. Distance Between Adjacent Intersections (default: 400) — Distance between the centers of 2 adjacent intersections (same row or same column). Important: The total number of intersections is always Rows × Columns — since every road axis runs the full length of the grid, you cannot get an arbitrary intersection count like 3, 5, 7 (unless it's a 1-row/column grid). The panel already shows a live info line with the actual intersection count, so you can cross-check it directly. 6. 🛣️ Lanes (per row/column) This is the most important group of fields — it drives the actual flight-path layout. Lanes Per Road Cluster (default: 4) — Number of lanes WITHIN each row/column of the grid — not the total lane count for the whole scene. Every 2 adjacent lanes pair up into 1 two-way "road". Default 4 = each row/column has 2 parallel two-way roads. Set to 2 for just 1 road per row/column. ALWAYS keep this an EVEN number — an odd number leaves 1 lane with no opposing pair. Number Of Altitude Levels (default: 3) — Number of flight levels by altitude (Z). Distance Between Lanes (default: 25) — Distance between 2 parallel lanes (2 DIFFERENT roads, not the two directions of the same road). Distance Between Levels (default: 20) — Vertical (Z) distance between 2 adjacent altitude levels. Lowest Level Altitude (Z) (default: 15) — Z altitude of the lowest level. Horizontal Offset Between Levels (default: 8) — Even/odd levels get an extra sideways offset along the perpendicular axis — creates a more natural zig-zag feel between levels. Two-Way Distance Within 1 Road (default: 8) — Distance between the 2 opposing lanes sitting right next to each other within the SAME road (e.g. lane 0 forward, lane 1 reverse, forming 1 pair). Should be much SMALLER than "Distance Between Lanes" (which is the distance to a DIFFERENT road). Extra Distance Between 2 Roads (default: 15) — An EXTRA gap (added on top of Distance Between Lanes) between 2 adjacent lane PAIRS (= 2 different roads) — not the distance between the two directions within the same road. When Split Into 3 Separate Streams is on , the last 6 fields (Dist. Lanes / Dist. Levels / Lowest Alt Z / Hor. Offset / 2-Way Dist. / Extra Dist.) each have a separate copy per stream — Civilian / Cargo / Military (shown as 3 columns) — since each ship type has a different size and therefore needs different spacing. ⚡ Auto-Fill From Ship Sizes (button) — Automatically recalculates 4 fields (Distance Between Lanes / Levels / Two-Way / Extra) based on the largest ship's width of each stream (measured perpendicular to the flight direction, not a 3D bounding radius) — and also lowers the Vertical/Horizontal Step Ratio (under Staggered Formation) to a safe ≤0.4 value if it's currently higher. This is a one-time action; you can freely edit the values afterward — Generate Traffic will NOT overwrite them again. "i Each adjacent lane pair..." info line — Reminder: every adjacent lane pair forms 1 two-way road. ShipProxy buttons (at the bottom of the Lanes section) Create ShipProxy (button) — Replaces ALL ships (every stream) with a lightweight box (a Geometry Nodes point cloud), spawned at each ship's current position. Used to quickly test the layout without touching the real (heavy) ship meshes. Click again anytime to rebuild the boxes at the ships' current position. Apply ShipProxy (button) — Only enabled while ShipProxy boxes exist. Removes the boxes, shows the real ships again, and (if Generate Traffic was run while the boxes existed) transfers the computed animation onto the matching real ships. Important: while ShipProxy is active, adjusting any Lanes/Streams/Formation field live-updates the box positions immediately — no extra action needed. And clicking ▶ Generate Traffic at this point runs on the boxes (fast), leaving the real ships untouched until you click Apply ShipProxy. 7. ✈️ Staggered Formation Controls how ships spread out in parallel formation within the same lane, instead of stacking into a single rigid line. Staggered Slots — Horizontal (default: 3) — Number of sideways offset positions (perpendicular to the flight direction) available in a lane's formation. Staggered Slots — Vertical (Z) (default: 3) — Number of offset positions along the Z axis in the formation. Vertical / Horizontal Step Ratio (default: 0.6) — The vertical (Z) offset step = this ratio × the horizontal offset step. Should generally stay below 1, since the vertical gap between levels (Distance Between Levels) is limited. If set too high, the addon automatically caps it — with a warning shown in the log when generating. Group Ships By Size (default: Off) — Off (default, same as previous versions): ships are spread across lanes in list order, and the formation's offset step is computed once from the LARGEST ship in the WHOLE stream — simple, and lets large and small ships mix together naturally. On: ships are first grouped by size (see the field below), each group gets its own lane(s), and each lane's offset step is computed only from the ships actually placed in it — keeps small-ship lanes tightly packed instead of matching the stream's largest ship, and reduces leftover collisions between very mismatched sizes. Size Grouping Threshold (%) (default: 50) — Only used when Group Ships By Size is on. Ships are grouped so that no ship's radius exceeds the group's smallest-ship radius by more than this percentage (e.g. 50 = up to 1.5× that group's smallest radius). Lower = tighter, more size-uniform groups (needs more lanes); higher = looser groups, closer to the Off behavior. Note: the "Ships have a FIXED offset..." info line is a reminder that the PRIMARY collision-avoidance mechanism today is spatial (a fixed formation offset), not the older time-stretching approach. 8. ⚡ Speed & Timing Minimum Speed / Maximum Speed (default: 0.7 / 1.5) — Random speed factor applied to each ship (combined with that stream's own Speed Factor, if Split Into 3 Streams is on). Frames To Cross Scene (Speed 1.0) (default: 650) — Number of frames it takes a ship to travel the full scene length, AT a speed factor of 1.0. This is an indirect way of setting actual speed: actual speed = (lane length) ÷ this value. Total Animation Frames (default: 700) — Every single ship's animation spans exactly from frame 0 to this frame — a ship is always flying through the central area at any moment within this range (including near the very last frame), with no "not yet appeared / already gone" gaps. Common issue: if the ratio of (lane length ÷ speed) is much larger than "Total Animation Frames", ships will look like "2 groups charging toward each other" at the start of the video before gradually mixing — this is not a bug, it's the natural consequence of a lane that's too long / a speed that's too slow relative to the video length. Quick fix: increase "Frames To Cross Scene" , or increase the Min/Max Speed. 9. 🌐 Scene Size Scene Radius (default: 150) — Radius of the boundary area — ships depart from and fly toward/beyond this boundary. Push Back Beyond Boundary (default: 20) — Ships depart/end an extra distance beyond the boundary above, rather than stopping exactly at the boundary. 10. 🏢 Building Avoidance Building Collision Margin (default: 5) — The BASE safety buffer around buildings — the addon automatically adds each ship's own actual width on top of this value when checking for a building collision, so this field only needs to be a small extra margin, not the ship's full size. Note: this is the only field in this section. If ships are still clipping or grazing a building, try increasing this value first; if increasing it a lot still doesn't help, buildings are likely placed too densely, leaving no lane with enough real clearance (check the warning line shown when generating: "N ship(s) still had a building-overlap risk..." ). 11. 🛸 Ship-Ship Collision Avoidance (Outer Edge) Safety Distance (Ship Hull Outer Edge) (default: 6) — Minimum GAP measured from the OUTER EDGE of the ship hull (not center-to-center like the old version) — the addon automatically adds each ship's own radius when: (1) checking space-time conflicts between ships, and (2) computing the staggered formation grid's offset step. Increasing this value does NOT stretch ships further apart along the lane — it only widens the sideways formation grid. Fallback Delay Step (Frames) (default: 20) — ONLY used when 2 ships land on the exact same formation slot — the PRIMARY collision-avoidance mechanism today is spatial (Staggered Formation), no longer mainly time-based. Max Delay Attempts (default: 30) — Maximum number of fallback delay attempts before the addon gives up and accepts the conflict. Tip: if the generate log reports "N ship(s) COULD NOT fully avoid collisions" , try increasing the Staggered Slots (section 7) or increasing Max Delay Attempts/Fallback Delay Step here. 12. ⚙️ Options Random Seed (default: 42) — Change this number to get a different ship layout (departure order, lane tie-break results when tied, random speed, etc.). The ship count and lane/level layout stay identical — only the random elements change. Ship Nose Axis (Local) (default: +Y) — The model's LOCAL axis that points toward the ship's nose (NOT the world-space flight direction!). In Object Mode, enable Local Axes display (N-panel or Viewport Overlays > Axes) to see which local axis the model's nose points along in that specific model, then pick that same axis here. If, after generating, ships fly "nose backwards" or "sideways", try changing this field. Interpolation Type (default: Linear (100% Match With UE)) — Interpolation type between position keyframes. Linear : constant motion, unchanging speed — exports to UE matching exactly regardless of which BlendReal mode is used ("Original Keyframes Only" or "Every Frame"). Bezier : smoother, with acceleration/deceleration at the start/end of each segment — ONLY matches UE exactly when BlendReal uses "Every Frame" mode; with "Original Keyframes Only", the UE result will be off because UE and Blender interpolate Bezier curves using different formulas. 13. 🔥 Spaceship Trail (Export to UE) Fields controlling the engine exhaust trail (Niagara trail) when exporting to Unreal Engine via the separate BlendReal addon (this is an independent addon — it only reads shared data through the Scene's custom properties). Enable Spaceship Trail (default: Off) — Master switch. When off, "Compute & Preview Trail Points" still works, but BlendReal will skip spawning any trail in UE. Niagara System Path (UE) (default: empty) — Content Browser path in UE to the Niagara System asset for the trail (e.g. /Game/VFX/NS_SpaceshipTrail ) — must already be built in UE beforehand. Trail Package Folder + search button (magnifier) — Scans an installed Content/Trail_Package folder on disk to find NS_SpaceshipTrail* Niagara System assets, for quick selection instead of typing the path by hand. Trail Height Ratio (default: 0.25) — Vertical attach position of the trail point, along the ship's local Z axis, 0 = bottom, 1 = top. Ignored if Nose Axis is Z/-Z, since Z is then the nose-to-tail axis itself. Trail Side Ratio (default: 1.0) — Sideways offset for a symmetric PAIR of trail points, as a ratio of that specific ship's own actual width (not a fixed number) — automatically scales correctly per ship size. 1.0 = right at the hull edge, <1.0 = inset, >1.0 = beyond the hull edge. 0 = a single trail point at the center. Ribbon Width Ratio (default: 10.0) — Trail ribbon width, as a ratio of the ship's own half-width — also scales automatically per ship. Hot Phase Duration (sec) (default: 0.3) — Real seconds (not a % of trail length) the white-hot → red engine glow lasts before fading to smoke — matches Niagara User.HotPhaseSeconds. Noise Intensity (default: 3.0) — Overall turbulence strength multiplier — matches Niagara User.NoiseIntensity. Trail Lifetime (sec) (default: 9.0) — Total particle lifetime = total visible trail length over time — matches Niagara User.TrailLifetime. Trail Opacity (default: 0.1) — Overall trail opacity multiplier — matches Niagara User.TrailOpacity. Civilian/Cargo/Military Trail Color (or Trail Color , if Split Into 3 Streams is off) (default: White, 1,1,1,1) — Trail tint per ship type — matches Niagara User.TrailColor. Recompute ALL Ships (default: Off, safe) — Off: "Compute & Preview Trail Points" only computes ships that do NOT yet have trail data — ships you've already hand-adjusted (e.g. multi-engine ships) are left untouched. On: forces a full recompute of EVERY ship, discarding any manual adjustments not yet Applied — asks for confirmation first. Compute & Preview Trail Points (button) — Computes marker positions and shows a preview for you to check and drag-adjust if needed. Clear Trail Preview (button) — Clears the current preview (without saving). Apply Trail Preview (button) — Locks in the marker positions (including any manual adjustments) — must be clicked before exporting to UE. Trail Include / Exclude list — List of individual ships or whole Collections explicitly turned ON or OFF for trail. Final result = Include minus Exclude (Exclude always wins). Both empty = no ship gets a trail. Refresh (button) — Refreshes the cached ship list used by both the Include/Exclude checklists. 14. Main action buttons (bottom of the panel, before the Preset section) ▶ Generate Traffic (button) — Runs the entire real pipeline — lane assignment, formation spreading, animation generation. This is the ONE accurate result, not a live preview. ✕ Clear (button) — Deletes the previously generated traffic/animation. 15. 📋 Config Preset Preset Name + save button (💾) — Name it, then save every current field value as a preset (saved to a JSON file on disk, not inside the .blend file). Load Preset (button) — Pick a saved preset and apply every field value from it. Delete (button) — Deletes a saved preset. "N preset(s) saved" line — Informational only. Good to know Every field value is saved PER SCENE, inside your .blend file — not in Blender's Preferences, nor inside the addon itself. A brand-new .blend file uses whatever default the addon ships with; a .blend file you've already saved keeps whatever value it was saved with, even after you update the addon to a newer version with different defaults. Presets (section 15) are saved to a separate JSON file on disk (not inside the .blend ) — so you can reuse the same preset across different .blend files. While ShipProxy is active, most fields under Lanes/Streams/Formation live-update as soon as you type a number , with no need to click Generate. Split Into 3 Separate Streams affects many other sections (Streams & Collections, Lanes showing 3 columns instead of 1, Trail showing 3 colors instead of 1) — if something looks different from what this guide describes, check whether this field is on or off first, since the layout of other sections changes quite a bit depending on it.
docs.title: Overview

docs.text: Procedural Blender add-on for spaceship traffic — automatically generates lane/intersection networks, avoids buildings by pre-checking real gaps between them so every ship flies a single straight line with zero mid-flight direction changes, and performs true ship-to-ship avoidance using a Space-Time Reservation system. Includes a flight path toolkit (7 NURBS Path presets + Follow Curve for Mesh or Camera), a shared Camera Track-To / Camera Shake / Bake Animation / Restore Constraint toolkit, mesh utilities, and an optional engine exhaust effect export to Unreal Niagara via BlendReal™. The add-on operates in Standalone Mode — Unreal Engine is not required — all traffic features run entirely within Blender. Alternatively, the Spaceship Trail (Export to UE) feature requires the BlendReal™ - Cinematic Pipeline UE5 add-on to automatically transfer Niagara parameter values into UE.
docs.title: BlendReal™ Spaceship Traffic

docs.text: Operating System: Windows 10/11 64-bit Blender : 4.5, 5.0, or 5.2 (LTS) Unreal Engine is not required for the main traffic features BlendReal™ (separate add-on) is required to use the Spaceship Trail feature

docs.text: In Blender, go to Edit > Preferences > Add-ons Click Install from Disk... and select the .zip file Tick the checkbox next to BlendReal™ Spaceship Traffic to enable the add-on Open the Sidebar (press N ) in the 3D Viewport and find the Spaceship Traffic tab
docs.title: 🛠️Installation

docs.text: Prepare Your Models : have your spaceship models ready (in .blend format, with one or several ships per file), along with building/obstacle models in the scene Create Collections : in the 📦 Streams & Collections section, click 🗂 Create Collections (Ships + Buildings) to automatically create the required Collections with the correct names (automatically based on whether "Split Into 3 Separate Streams" is on/off) Import Ships : still in 📦 Streams & Collections — select the folder containing the spaceship .blend files in Ship File Folder , choose which stream to import them into ( Import Into Stream ), then click 📥 Import Ships From Folder . Ships can all sit on top of each other at the origin at this point — Generate Traffic will redistribute them automatically Add Buildings to the Collection : manually drag and drop the building objects into the created Collection in the Outliner Click ⚡ Auto-Fill From Ship Sizes (inside the 🛣️ Lanes section) — this is the recommended first step : the add-on automatically computes most of the lane/altitude spacing values based on the actual size of your imported ships instead of you guessing numbers by hand. Everything stays freely editable afterward — Generate Traffic will NOT overwrite these values Preview the layout (optional) : also inside 🛣️ Lanes , click 👁 Create ShipProxy , then adjust the Lane/Streams/Formation fields to see whether the ship placeholder boxes are arranged the way you want (see Live Layout Preview below) Click ▶ Generate Traffic — the add-on automatically generates animation for all ships, with real building and ship avoidance To start over: click ✕ Clear Animation To view the system report: click 🔍 Check Collections (found inside Streams & Collections; output is displayed in the System Console) 💡 Tip for new users : if you don't want to hand-tune every parameter, simply follow Import Ships → Auto-Fill From Ship Sizes → Generate Traffic and you'll immediately get a reasonable traffic layout. The sections below are only needed when you want to fine-tune things further.

docs.text: 7 built-in shapes, spawned right at the selected object's location (or at the 3D Cursor if nothing is selected): Straight , Arc , Loop , S-Curve , Zigzag , Spiral , Figure-8 . After creation, adjust the parameters in the "Adjust Last Operation" panel (bottom-left): - Size — overall length (Straight/Arc/S-Curve/Zigzag) or radius (Loop/Spiral/Figure-8) - Points — number of NURBS control points, higher = smoother curve - Forward Axis — which local axis the path primarily travels along - Arc Angle — Arc only: how many degrees the arc sweeps - Amplitude / Wave Cycles — S-Curve/Zigzag only: how far the path swings side to side, and how many oscillations - Turns / Height — Spiral only: number of full rotations and total distance travelled Follow Curve : select exactly 1 mesh or camera + 1 curve (any order), then click — automatically adds a Follow Path constraint (named "BlendReal Follow Path"), along with Curve Resolution (how smooth the curve itself is). You only need to keyframe the 2 values that appear right below while that object is selected: Follow Path Distance (actual distance in Blender units, not a 0–1 ratio) and Follow Path Tilt (additional banking angle). 🎥 Camera-specific behavior : if the followed object is a Camera, Follow Path only drives its POSITION along the curve — it does not rotate the camera to match the curve's tangent, and Follow Path Tilt has no visible effect. This is on purpose: it leaves 100% of the aim/rotation to whatever the Camera already has (typically a Track To constraint from Create Camera Track-To Constraint , see the Bake Animation section below), so the camera keeps looking exactly where you pointed it while still flying along the curve. ⚠️ The Bake Auto Bank feature (automatically computing the banking angle from the curve's curvature) is currently an internal work-in-progress (WIP) and is not shown in the panel in this build — for now, adjust Tilt manually via keyframes.
docs.title: 🛤️ NURBS Path Presets

docs.text: Remove Constraint After Bake — after baking, automatically removes the original Constraint(s) (Follow Path, Track To...) to avoid double-transform conflicts; disable this if you still need to edit the Constraint(s) afterward Bake Animation — bakes Location/Rotation/Scale of any selected Mesh, Camera, or Empty into real keyframes with one click, automatically backing up every supported Constraint present on the object before baking (e.g. a Camera using both Follow Path + Track To together — not just one of them) Restore Baked Constraint — restores all the original Constraint(s) + Target(s) + Action from before the last bake (only works on objects previously baked via the button above); this data is shared with BlendReal™ - Cinematic Pipeline UE5 , so baking in one add-on can be restored from the other Create Camera Track-To Constraint — one click creates a Camera + a target Empty (named "CameraTarget") with a Track To constraint already set up between them (more stable than Damped Track during live preview); shared feature also found in BlendReal™ - Cinematic Pipeline UE5 Add Camera Shake — adds a short, keyframed handheld-style shake to the selected Camera starting at the current frame, with Amplitude , Frequency , Pulses , and Target Shake Ratio (if the Camera has a Track To / Damped Track constraint, its target Empty shakes too — phase-shifted by 1/4 cycle so the aim direction wobbles naturally instead of staying locked dead-on target; set to 0 to shake only the Camera). Re-running this on an overlapping frame range replaces the previous shake there automatically
docs.title: 🎬 Bake Animation (Location/Rotation/Scale)

docs.text: Apply Rotation / Apply Scale — applies in batch to multiple selected meshes at once, keeping the other 2 values unchanged (Location is always preserved by both buttons) Apply Naming (Island/Building/Landscape) — batch renames using a standard prefix, opening a dialog with: Type — Floating Island ( Island_ ) / Building ( Building_ ) / Landscape ( Landscape_ ) / Custom Prefix (your own prefix, no automatic Tag/Collision assignment) Base Name — the name part after the prefix (e.g. "FloatingIsland" → Island_FloatingIsland01 , 02 ...) Custom Prefix — only used when Type = Custom Start Index / Digit Count — the starting number and zero-padding digit count (2 digits: 01, 02...; 3 digits: 001, 002...) Fix Normals Per UV Island — recalculates normals per UV island in a radial outward direction (based on the object's center of mass, independent of topology) — handles cases where Blender's default Recalculate Outside / Merge+Recalculate fail Create Proxy Collision (Convex Hull) — duplicates meshes named with this convention, splits them by connected "island" pieces, with 2 Method options: Convex Hull Per Piece (recommended) — always clean regardless of how broken the source mesh is, preserves concavities between pieces Voxel Remesh (fallback) — rebuilds the surface via a distance field, with extra [Voxel] Resolution , [Voxel] Adaptivity , [Voxel] Weld Vertices Before Remesh , [Voxel] Merge Distance parameters The result is named so UE automatically recognizes it as Collision
docs.title: 🔧 Mesh Utilities — standalone, no BlendReal™ required

docs.text: Split Into 3 Separate Streams (Civilian / Cargo / Military) — on (default): each ship type is pulled from its own Collection, flying its own altitude band and speed factor, never mixing, while still sharing one Space-Time Reservation ledger so they still avoid each other correctly at stream crossing points. Off: falls back to a single shared ship Collection Civilian / Cargo / Military Collection + a Speed × multiplier for each stream (default Civilian ×0.85, Cargo ×0.6, Military ×1.35 — applied on top of the shared Minimum/Maximum Speed) Distance Between Streams — the horizontal offset (top view, X axis) between the 3 stream areas: Civilian on the left, Cargo in the middle, Military on the right, each with its own non-overlapping intersection grid Building Collection — the Collection containing buildings/obstacles 🗂 Create Collections (Ships + Buildings) — automatically creates the required Collections (using the names set in the fields above) if they don't already exist 🔍 Check Collections — prints a system report to the System Console Import Into Stream + Ship File Folder (.blend) + 📥 Import Ships From Folder — batch imports every ship from all .blend files in a folder into the Collection of the chosen stream, with a progress bar + elapsed time counter in the viewport, automatically skipping Cameras/Lights, and remembering previously imported files to prevent duplicates
docs.title: 📦 Streams & Collections

docs.text: Number Of Rows (Y) / Number Of Columns (X) — the number of rows/columns of the intersection grid. The actual number of intersections is ALWAYS Rows × Columns (since every road axis runs the full length of the grid, you can't get an arbitrary intersection count like 3, 5, 7 unless the grid has only 1 row/column) Distance Between Adjacent Intersections — the distance between the centers of 2 adjacent intersections (same row or same column)
docs.title: 🚦 Intersection Grid (per stream)

docs.text: Lanes Per Road Cluster — the number of lanes in EACH row/column of the grid (not the total lane count for the whole scene) — always use an EVEN number, since every 2 adjacent lanes pair up into 1 two-way "road" Number Of Altitude Levels — the number of altitude (Z) levels flying simultaneously within one stream When 3 Streams is on, the 6 spacing fields below get separate columns for Civilian / Cargo / Military : Dist. Lanes (Distance Between Lanes) — the distance between 2 neighboring two-way "roads" Dist. Levels (Distance Between Levels) — the spacing between 2 adjacent altitude levels Lowest Alt Z (Lowest Level Altitude) — the lowest altitude, used as the base the levels above stack on Hor. Offset (Horizontal Offset Between Levels) — the alternating horizontal offset between even/odd levels, for a more natural layout 2-Way Dist. (Two-Way Distance Within 1 Road) — the distance between the 2 opposing lanes within the SAME road — should be set MUCH smaller than Distance Between Lanes Extra Dist. (Extra Distance Between 2 Roads) — an EXTRA gap (on top of Distance Between Lanes) between 2 adjacent lane pairs ⚡ Auto-Fill From Ship Sizes (recommended): a one-time action — automatically fills Distance Between Lanes / Distance Between Levels / Two-Way Distance / Extra Distance for each stream based on its largest ship's radius, and lowers the Vertical/Horizontal Step Ratio to a safe value (≤0.4) so Vertical Staggered Slot never gets clamped, regardless of ship size. Lowest Level Altitude Z is stacked in order Civilian → Cargo → Military (each step taking the LARGER of Distance Between Streams or the stream-below's own vertical span) — guaranteeing no altitude overlap between streams without an oversized gap for normal-sized fleets. Horizontal Offset Between Levels is copied as-is from Civilian (purely cosmetic, not size-related). Everything stays freely editable afterward — Generate Traffic will NOT overwrite these values again.
docs.title: 🛣️ Lanes (per row/column)

docs.text: 👁 Create ShipProxy — creates lightweight proxy boxes sized exactly to each ship, at each ship's current position; the real ships are temporarily hidden Once the boxes exist, adjust any Lane/Streams/Formation field — the layout updates live on the boxes You can also click ▶ Generate Traffic while previewing — the add-on runs the full collision-avoidance pass ON THE BOXES (faster than running it on real, detailed-mesh ships), while still using the ships' REAL radius for safety calculations ✅ Apply ShipProxy — once you're happy with it, brings back the real ships and applies the final result to them 💡 This is a tool for previewing a reasonable layout — the final, accurate result always comes from clicking ▶ Generate Traffic on the real ships (via Apply ShipProxy, or directly if you're not using the preview).
docs.title: 👁️ Live Layout Preview (lives inside the Lanes section)

docs.text: Staggered Slots — Horizontal / — Vertical (Z) — the number of horizontal/vertical offset positions in a lane's staggered formation, letting multiple ships share a lane without overlapping Vertical / Horizontal Step Ratio — the vertical (Z) step = this ratio × the horizontal step — usually kept below 1, since the Z gap between levels is limited Group Ships By Size — OFF (default, same as previous versions): the staggered step is computed once from the largest ship radius in the WHOLE stream. ON: ships are first grouped by size (see Size Grouping Threshold (%) — e.g. 50 = up to 1.5x that group's smallest radius), tightening the Staggered Formation spacing per lane based on whichever ships actually ended up there, instead of always sizing for the stream's single largest ship ℹ️ When buildings exist in the scene , Gap-Fit (see Building Avoidance below) already assigns ships to lanes by their real size automatically — Group Ships By Size no longer decides which lane a ship goes to in that case, but it still tightens the Staggered Formation spacing per lane the same way described above.
docs.title: ✈️ Staggered Formation

docs.text: Minimum Speed / Maximum Speed — the random speed-factor range applied to each ship (further multiplied by the per-stream Speed ×) Frames To Cross Scene (Speed 1.0) — the reference number of frames to travel the full scene length at speed factor 1.0 Total Animation Frames — every ship's animation spans exactly from frame 0 to this value ⚠️ Important note when increasing speed : if you push speed much higher relative to Total Animation Frames, a ship may finish flying its entire lane in just a few dozen frames while the displayed timeline is several hundred or thousand frames long — that ship will "flash by" quickly, then sit FROZEN for most of the remaining timeline, making it look like "most ships aren't moving." This isn't a bug — if you want to see many ships moving clearly throughout the video, keep speed moderate or shorten Total Animation Frames accordingly.
docs.title: ⚡ Speed & Timing

docs.text: Scene Radius — ships depart from and arrive beyond this radius Push Back Beyond Boundary — the extra distance ships start out/end beyond the Scene Radius boundary
docs.title: 🌐 Scene Size

docs.text: Every ship flies exactly 1 straight line, with zero direction changes mid-flight — building avoidance is entirely decided before a ship starts moving, not reacted to along the way: For every lane, the add-on sweeps its full length and works out the narrowest real gap between buildings that a ship would have to pass through — accounting for the Building Collision Margin AND the worst-case sideways reach of the Staggered Formation (so a ship can never be nudged into a building it was assigned to safely clear) Each ship is only assigned to a lane whose gap is wide enough for its own width, widest ships first, spread across the least-used valid lanes If NO lane in the grid is wide enough for a ship (e.g. an oversized capital ship in a dense building cluster), the add-on automatically creates a Boundary Lane just outside the entire building cluster's footprint and routes it there instead — guaranteed clear, at the same altitude levels as normal traffic A building sitting directly on a lane's centerline (a true dead end, not just a tight squeeze) removes that lane from consideration entirely, the same way as an insufficient gap Building Collision Margin — the safety buffer kept around every building's actual bounds, used throughout the gap calculation above
docs.title: 🏢 Building Avoidance

docs.text: Safety Distance (Ship Hull Outer Edge) — the minimum gap measured from the ship's OUTER HULL edge (not center-to-center) — the add-on automatically adds each ship's actual radius (from its bounding box) both when checking space-time conflicts AND when computing the staggered formation's offset step. Increasing this value does NOT stretch ships further apart along the lane — it only widens the staggered formation grid Fallback Delay Step (Frames) — ONLY used when 2 ships would land on the exact same staggered-formation slot (the primary avoidance mechanism is spatial, not time-based) Max Delay Attempts — how many fallback delay attempts before accepting the conflict After Generate Traffic , the add-on clearly reports the number of ships that could not fully avoid collisions + suggests which parameter to increase.
docs.title: 🛸 Ship-Ship Collision Avoidance (Outer Edge)

docs.text: Random Seed — change to get a different ship layout Ship Nose Axis (Local) — the local axis the ship's nose points along (enable local axis display in the N-panel or Viewport Overlays > Axes to see the correct axis; change this if the ship flies "nose backwards" or "sideways" after Generate) Interpolation Type — Linear (100% match when exported to UE via BlendReal, in both export modes) or Bezier (smoother, with ease in/out — but only matches exactly when BlendReal uses "Every Frame" mode)
docs.title: ⚙️ Options

docs.text: Enable Spaceship Trail — the master switch for the trail feature Niagara System Path (UE) — the Content Browser path to the pre-built Niagara System in UE; can be found via Trail Package Folder + Scan for Trail Systems to automatically scan and pick Trail Height Ratio / Trail Side Ratio — where the trail attaches, vertically and side-to-side, scaled to each ship's OWN actual size Ribbon Width Ratio — the ribbon width, also scaled to each ship's own actual size Niagara Look (User Parameters) : Hot Phase Duration (how long the white-hot → red glow lasts before fading to smoke), Noise Intensity (turbulence), Trail Lifetime (total trail length in time), Trail Opacity , plus individual trail colors per stream (or one shared color when 3 Streams is off) 🔄 Refresh Ship List , Include/Exclude lists (pick individual ships or whole Collections, live-linked — Exclude always wins), Recompute ALL Ships (OFF by default — safe, only computes ships without data yet; turn on to force a full recompute, with confirmation first) Compute & Preview Trail Points — automatically computes trail attachment points from each ship's bounding box + Nose Axis, shown as draggable Empty markers (paired markers auto-sync) Clear Trail Preview Markers , Apply Marker Positions to Export Data — writes the final positions into the export data
